subject: Streaming handback — throughput extract & SLO synthesis
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@fleetai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming handback — throughput extract & SLO synthesis

Hi Amit — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick post-call recap and the follow-up asks we agreed:

1) Goal: confirm SLOs for the streaming inference path for FleetAI pilot (video frame -> short-form summary).
2) Inputs you promised: average tokens per event (we have a proxy), peak concurrent streams during promotions, TTL for KV caching per session.
3) Redwood asks: sample 1-hour traffic trace (preferred) or event-rate histogram; expected tail latency SLO; SLA/penalty sensitivity.

Initial notes based on what you shared verbally:
- Typical per-event output: ~220 tokens (median) / 95th pct ~420 tokens.
- Median request rate from edge: 70 QPS baseline across pipelines, but peaks to ~2,800 QPS during ingress bursts (15–20s crests).
- Active concurrent streams: typically 120 steady, cresting to 1,100 for short windows.

Preliminary sizing (very conservative):
- Sustained baseline: ~70 QPS * 220 tokens = ~15.4k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Peak crest: 2,800 QPS * 420 tokens = ~1,176k tokens/sec.
- Target latency SLO (streaming end-to-end): 95th token latency <= 180ms; absolute tail <= 500ms for first token.

What we recommend next (deliverables):
- FleetAI: share 1-hour sample trace (timestamps + event token estimates) or permission for Redwood to collect via test webhook.
- Redwood: deliver a short throughput extract (spreadsheet) and 2 capacity options: cost-lean steady-state and burst-resilient reserve. Attached is the worksheet we will fill in once we have the trace.

Next steps / owners:
- Amit: send sample trace or confirm webhook collection by EOD Wednesday.
- Logan: produce quantitative throughput extract and two capacity options (ETA: 24 hours after receiving trace).
- Marissa/Karthik: review sizing notes and confirm canary and fallback model variants for burst handling.

Attachment: fleetai_streaming_profile.pdf (workshop notes) and 20280720_fleetai_throughput_estimate.xlsx (empty template).

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up 30m if you want to walk the worksheet together.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Amit Shah <amit@fleetai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@fleetai.com
Date: 2028-07-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming handback — throughput extract & SLO synthesis

Appreciate the recap, Logan. A few clarifications from our side before you size: 

- The token estimate you used (median 220, p95 420) is in-line with our offline samples — good call.
- For one-hour trace: I can send anonymized event timestamps + estimated tokens per event. Will strip PII. Expect to drop this into your S3 by EOD.
- Regarding peaks: those 2,800 QPS bursts are usually multi-tenant — but note 40% of crest traffic comes from a single customer during marketing pushes.
- Latency expectation: we care about end-to-end user-perceived latency. If Redwood can keep 95th token latency under 200ms consistently in our eu-west region, that's 👍. For initial pilot in us-west, 180ms is preferable.

One ask: can you model an alternate scenario where KV cache is cold (i.e., no prefix cached) vs warmed (50% hits)? That's our main operational risk.

I'll upload the sample trace to the link you provided tonight.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
Head of Ops, FleetAI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@fleetai.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming handback — throughput extract & SLO synthesis

Looping in our sizing leads. Quick operational framing and what I'll model: 

- Two scenarios: (A) steady-state baseline with aggressive batching and prefix caching; (B) burst-resilient with autoscale and fallback to compact model variant (quantized).
- Assumptions I'm starting with for the spreadsheet:
  • Model variant: RL-Streamer-Medium (fp16) — baseline tokens/sec on A100-ish: ~120k tokens/sec per GPU under optimal batching for batched requests.
  • Quantized compact fallback: ~260k tokens/sec effective (due to smaller context switches) but with 5–8% quality delta.
  • KV cache warm hit improvement: 30–55% token savings depending on median session length. We'll model 0%, 50%, 75% hit rates.
- Concurrency mapping: mapping steady 120 active streams -> estimated concurrency of 80 workers; crest 1,100 streams -> concurrency ~720 (depends on multiplexing and streaming protocol).

I will populate the attached workbook with three tabs: baseline, crest, cost-comparison (reserved vs burst on-demand). ETA to you after we get the trace: 24 hours.

Marissa
Director, Performance Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@fleetai.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming handback — throughput extract & SLO synthesis

Thanks — small ops/implementation notes we should include in the deliverable so Amit can hand to infra: 

- Ingress shaping: recommend a soft token-bucket at the edge (client-side) to absorb 10–20s crests. Document the burst budget we’ll need for 95th/99th windows.
- Model routing policy: primary -> RL-Streamer-Medium; fallback -> RL-Streamer-Compact-Quant (quantized). Automate rollback if quality drop > 7% on eval set.
- Streaming protocol: prefer HTTP/2 server push or gRPC stream with chunk-level ACKs; minimizes head-of-line blocking vs naive HTTP1 chunking.
- Telemetry hooks: require request_id, session_id, and partial-token timestamps to compute 95th token latency. Add that to the workbook's telemetry appendix.

I'll review Marissa's filled worksheet and align on the canary thresholds before we share final Sizing + Ops playbook with FleetAI.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
